Next month's 26th marks the one-year anniversary of the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee investigating the fire is expected to submit a report to the Chief Executive before the end of October. Recent reports indicated that the government has launched a directorate accountability investigation into the administrative responsibility for the blaze and transferred political assistants to assist. Chief Executive John Lee today (the 6th) did not respond to whether the mechanism has been activated, stating that the government has made a series of arrangements and will implement reforms and pursue accountability as soon as possible after the report is submitted. The luxury residence One Stanley in Stanley was exposed for having reinforcing steel that did not match the plans. Lee said the Buildings Department is investigating the case and has requested the Development Bureau to oversee the investigation. As multiple construction projects have been exposed for problems one after another, he said he attaches importance to the quality of construction in Hong Kong, which concerns the professional standards, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will strictly enforce the law.

It has been nearly a year since the Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee is expected to submit a report before the end of October. (File photo)

Earlier media reports stated that two political assistants, former Deputy Secretary for Security Mok Kwan-yu and Commissioner for Sports Choi Kin-bun, would provide support to an investigation小组 under the Public Service Commission, specifically tasked with preliminary work on administrative accountability.

Chief Executive John Lee attended a press conference before the Executive Council meeting today and was asked whether the reports were true? Whether the activation of the directorate accountability investigation into responsibility means that even with a report, if official accountability is involved, there will not be immediate results — how long must the public wait?

Lee stated that he made it clear from the start that after the independent committee submits its report, he will actively study and follow up on its recommendations, implement reforms and announce details. He did not directly respond to whether political assistants have already been transferred to prepare for the preliminary investigation work, only saying that "the government has made a series of arrangements during this period," emphasising that after the report is submitted, based on its contents, he will "implement comprehensive reforms and pursue accountability as soon as possible in the short term," with a detailed announcement to be made at that time.

Lee stated that after the independent committee submits its report, reforms and accountability will be pursued as soon as possible based on the report's contents. (File photo)

Lee also reiterated multiple times that improvement measures cannot wait. Therefore, when delivering the Policy Address in September, he announced 7 priority improvement measures, including: banning smoking at construction sites, strengthening regulation of fire service installations, enhancing disciplinary actions against professionals and contractors, improving compliance in owners' corporations, studying the criminalisation of bid-rigging, providing tendering and evaluation services for the first time, establishing prequalification lists for consultants and contractors, and studying solutions to better assist the public in projects involving professional expertise.

According to records, the Public Service Commission is an independent statutory advisory body that advises the Chief Executive on civil service appointments, promotions and disciplinary matters. The directorate accountability system was proposed by Chief Executive John Lee in last year's Policy Address, establishing a two-tier investigation mechanism based on the severity of departmental issues. If the issue is less serious or involves a single incident, the first-tier investigation will be conducted by the department head. If the department has serious problems, or involves widespread, recurring systemic issues, or may involve the role of the department head, a second-tier investigation will be launched by an investigation小组 led by the Public Service Commission.

The luxury residence One Stanley was exposed for having units where reinforcing steel did not match the plans. Lee said he would not comment on cases still under investigation and has requested the Development Bureau to oversee the Buildings Department's investigation.

One Stanley 'reinforcement issue' — Development Bureau requested to oversee investigation

Recently, construction projects have been exposed for problems one after another, including: lift shaft tilting in the new block of Queen Mary Hospital, concrete sample strength not meeting standards at a Tung Chung public housing estate, and floor slab reinforcing steel not matching plans at the luxury residence One Stanley in Stanley. When asked whether there are problems in construction and even project supervision, Lee responded:

In response to the One Stanley project issues, he stated that the Buildings Department is conducting a serious investigation, "ascertaining whether construction quality and supervision were adequate, and will handle it strictly in accordance with the law." As the investigation is still ongoing, he would not comment on the case details, and has requested the Development Bureau to oversee the case investigation. However, he emphasised that he attaches importance to the construction quality of Hong Kong's building projects, "paying attention to whether professionals related to the projects have diligently supervised, and whether contractors have violated regulations during construction," and stated that it concerns the professional standards, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will inevitably enforce the law strictly.

He has also requested the Development Bureau to enhance regulatory requirements and penalties regarding legal aspects for overall construction projects, ensuring the deterrent effect of legislation, severely punishing relevant personnel who violate regulations, and safeguarding the professional standards, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction projects. The Development Bureau will submit proposed amendments to the Buildings Ordinance this year to strengthen supervision and enhance the disciplinary system and penalties, and the authorities will推进 this work at full speed.

The difficulty for nursing graduates in finding jobs has recently attracted attention. Lee stated that demand for nurses has long existed, and pointed out that the Hospital Authority currently has over 3,000 nurse vacancies that graduates can apply for. (File photo)

Executive Councillor Cheung Yu-man criticises 'unions impersonating people' — Lee states demand has long existed

Discussion about the difficulty for nurses in finding jobs has heated up recently. The trigger was a phone-in programme on a radio station after the Policy Address, in which a Mr. Kwok, who claimed to be a psychiatric nurse in a disciplinary force, said his application for deferred retirement was not approved, and that his daughter, a nursing graduate, was unemployed immediately after graduation, questioning the Hospital Authority's importation of Mainland medical personnel. Executive Councillor Cheung Yu-man subsequently questioned whether it was the union "impersonating people to make phone calls," and expressed his wholehearted support for importing talent from outside.

When asked by reporters about the difficulty for nursing graduates in finding jobs, how to address the concentration of vacancies among experienced nurses, and how to respond to Executive Councillor's remarks being accused of exacerbating social tensions, Lee stated that in every industry, there are cases where graduates do not immediately seek employment for various reasons, or where employers select those most suitable for their needs, "resulting in situations where some individuals are not hired." He emphasised that societal demand for nurses has always existed, especially with Hong Kong's continuously developing medical sector and the trend of an ageing population, "so recruitment numbers will ultimately inevitably reflect this existing demand." He also said, without naming anyone, that "there are different discussions in society on this aspect, which allows everyone to discuss the issues more clearly."

Lee also stated that according to 2025/26 figures, there are approximately 4,000 potential nursing graduates, with about 2,500 actually applying to the Hospital Authority, meaning 1,500 applied for positions outside the Hospital Authority. The Hospital Authority currently still has over 3,000 nurse vacancies, "nursing graduates can apply, and there is a chance of being hired."

Secretary for Health Professor Lo Chung-mau earlier在接受 multiple media interviews clarified that the government's recruitment policy definitely prioritises local talent. Lee also reiterated that based on the Hospital Authority's current number of nurses, "99.8% are locally trained nurses in Hong Kong," clearly implementing the policy of prioritising local talent in employment. He also pointed out that currently 40% of nurses work in the public healthcare system, with the remaining 60% in other medical positions, such as community nursing, elderly care, rehabilitation services, and private medical institutions. He emphasised that societal demand for nurses has long existed, and the government will, according to medical service needs, exchange views with the industry and academia, and do a good job in planning medical training and manpower development.
